title: Canned Meat Tortellini in Tomato Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Tortellini are small ring-shaped pasta filled with a seasoned meat blend of beef, pork, or a mixture of both. In the can they are immersed in a flavorful tomato sauce that preserves the taste and makes the dish ready to eat after heating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortellini originate from Italy, where they are traditionally served with butter sauce or in broth.
Canned tortellini appeared in the mid‑20th century as a convenient way to store ready‑to‑eat meals without refrigeration.
The tomato sauce often includes herbs such as basil, oregano, and garlic for extra aroma.
A typical 300 g can contains roughly 30‑40 individual tortellini.
Canned tortellini are popular for camping and school lunches because of their long shelf life.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat filling provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tortellini contain B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates from the pasta provide fast‑acting energy, useful during physical activity.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The meat filling can be relatively fatty, so those monitoring fat intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat‑based dough contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some cans may contain food preservatives that can cause individual sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Open the can, heat the contents in the microwave or on the stove until hot, stir, and serve. Tortellini can be added to soups, casseroles, or used as a quick pasta base.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the leftovers in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days.
